lesson.text: Quick memory: what is a pixel? (One small square of colour in a picture made on a grid.) Today: mosaics, pictures made of tiny tiles, thousands of years before pixels.
A mosaic is a picture or pattern made of small pieces of stone, glass or tile, called tesserae, set close together. The gaps between them are filled with grout.
The Romans made mosaic floors for their houses and baths: patterns, animals, sea creatures and scenes of daily life, from little cubes of coloured stone.
Worked example: plan it on squared paper, one square for each tile. This panel is 8 tiles wide and 5 tiles tall, so it needs 8 × 5 = 40 tiles.
Set the tiles in rows that follow the shape's outline, like water flowing round it. Mosaic makers call this flow andamento, and it makes a mosaic look alive.
Keep small, even gaps between the tiles. Choose colours that stand out against each other, like a dark shape on a light background. Then the picture reads from far away.
Mosaics come from many places: walls of glittering gold glass in Ravenna, Italy; geometric tiles called zellige in Morocco; and bright broken-tile mosaics on buildings today.
Try it in the world: make a mosaic floor in your world from coloured blocks, one block for each tile. Plan it on squared paper first, and give it a border. Next: architecture.

exercises.prompt: What are the small pieces of a mosaic called?
exercises.hint: It is a Latin word, used since Roman times.
exercises.explain: The small tiles of a mosaic are called tesserae.

exercises.prompt: Grout fills the gaps between the tiles of a mosaic.
exercises.hint: What goes in the thin lines between the tiles?
exercises.explain: True: grout fills the gaps and holds the tiles firm.

exercises.prompt: How many tiles are in this mosaic?
exercises.hint: Count the rows, and the tiles in one row.

exercises.prompt: Match each word to its meaning.
exercises.hint: Think of how a mosaic is made.
exercises.explain: Tesserae are the tiles, grout fills the gaps, andamento is the flow of the rows, and a border frames it.

exercises.prompt: How many white tiles are in this mosaic?
exercises.hint: Count row by row, touching each white tile.

exercises.prompt: A mosaic is 12 tiles wide and 9 tiles tall, with no gaps in the pattern. How many tiles does it need?
exercises.hint: Rows of tiles: how many rows, how many in each?

exercises.prompt: Which colours would make a dark blue fish stand out best?
exercises.hint: A shape stands out when it is very different from what is round it.
exercises.explain: Dark blue on pale yellow has the most contrast, so the fish shows clearly from far away.

exercises.prompt: Put the steps of making a mosaic in order.
exercises.hint: Grout goes in last, once every tile is down.
items: Stick them down with small gaps
Draw a plan on squared paper
exercises.explain: Plan it, choose colours, get the tiles ready, stick them down with gaps, then grout.

exercises.prompt: Roman floor mosaics were often made of little cubes of coloured stone.
exercises.hint: Think of what lasts under people's feet.
exercises.explain: True: small stone cubes were strong enough to walk on for centuries.

exercises.prompt: How many tiles are in the border?
exercises.hint: Count all the tiles, then take away the tiles inside the border.

exercises.prompt: A square mosaic has 10 tiles along each side. How many tiles are in a border one tile wide?
exercises.hint: All the tiles, take away the square inside (2 fewer each way).

exercises.prompt: Why do mosaic makers plan on squared paper first?
exercises.hint: Think of the worked example: one square, one tile.
choices: Each square stands for one tile
The paper is stuck into the mosaic
It is the only paper allowed
exercises.explain: Each square stands for one tile, so they can count the tiles and place every colour before they start.

exercises.prompt: What does andamento mean in a mosaic?
exercises.hint: It is an Italian word for how something goes or flows.
choices: the flow of the rows of tiles
exercises.explain: Andamento is the flow of the rows of tiles, following the shapes like water.

exercises.prompt: A mosaic of 1 cm tiles, 30 cm by 20 cm, needs about 600 tiles.
exercises.hint: How many tiles fit along each side?
